newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products mostly firm, holiday saps trade.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products mostly firm, holiday saps trade.

text.p: Trade in Mediterranean oil products was subdued on Monday with holidays in Italy and Spain.

Naphtha showed signs of a second decade recovery in prices. An Algerian cargo was heard offered at cif high +$3 a tonne. One dealer said Libyan and Egyptian term contract material was done "in excess of $3 above quotes," - an incentive to hold for higher numbers.
Gasoline prices recovered from late fall on Friday and were pegged notionally firmer on the back of strong NYMEX unleaded.
But traders said that despite an open arbitrage from the West Med to the U.S., holidays dulled activity.
Physical prices were marked a couple of dollars firmer to around $221/$224, cif Lavera.

Gas oil rose $4 a tonne in line with futures. The return of most traders from holiday injected modest demand into heating oil, supporting premiums at levels quoted on Friday of around cif high quotes +$2 basis Genoa.
But traders disagreed on how far premiums could rise. "People are trying to talk the market back up but I'm not all that optimistic," a trader said.
Demand emerged for heating oil for delivery into Greece and Yugoslavia.
A cargo of one percent sulphur was offered out of Lavera and a cargo of low sulphur diesel was offered loading Jannuary 20-30 out of Lavera.
High sulphur fuel oil cargo prices were firmer as an ARA player sold bunker fuel to an Iberian refiner at a hefty $126 cif Canaries..
Low sulphur fuel oil was hardly firmer, despite soaring crude, and players said they thought the market was long, while expecting little new demand out of Italy for January.
